BiblicalUsage: Ptysma means spittle, saliva. It appears once, in the healing of the man born blind: Jesus spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and He anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the clay of spittle is the Creator at work again: the same hands that formed man from the dust formed sight from the dust a second time.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
